## Context: what already exists (READ IT FIRST, it is the foundation)

The base package `fuzzsim/` provides:

energy (it returns calculate_score(entry) = AFL's constant schedule) and
`fuzz_one`/`select_next` are the extension points for scheduling.

1. DO NOT modify any existing file: not `fuzzsim/afl_fuzzer.py`, not
   `fuzzsim/experiments/afl_experiment.py`, not `run.sh`, not anything under
   `fuzzsim/targets/`, `fuzzsim/mutation.py`, `fuzzsim/seed.py`,
   `fuzzsim/bitmap.py`, `fuzzsim/program_model.py`, not `requirements/`.
   Subclass / compose instead. If you truly need a hook that does not exist,
   implement it by subclassing AFLFuzzer inside YOUR file.
2. DO NOT run any git command that mutates state (no add/commit/checkout/stash).
   Read-only git (log/diff/show) is fine. I handle commits.
3. Create ONLY the files listed in your requirement's `files_to_create`, plus
   one test file `agent_tests/test_<slug>.py`. Nothing else.
4. Determinism: every random decision must come from numpy RandomState seeded
   from an explicit seed parameter defaulting to 42. No time/os.urandom/Math.random.
   Running the experiment twice must print identical output.
5. Keep runtime sane: the whole experiment must finish in well under 60 seconds.
6. Match the code style of `fuzzsim/afl_fuzzer.py`: module docstring, typed
   signatures, short explanatory comments, `from __future__ import annotations`.

## Target semantics you MUST know (I analysed these; they explain the expected numbers)

CrashmeProgram (30 edges):
- Edges reachable by NON-crashing executions: {0..15, 17..24, 27, 29} = exactly
  26 edges. 26/30 = 86.666..% -> "86.7". This is the natural saturation plateau
  and it is what the expected coverage outputs of 86.7 mean.
- Edge 28 is unreachable (never emitted by execute()).
- Edges 16 and 25 are hit ONLY on crash path 1 (b0%3==2, b1%2==0,
  0x30<=b2<=0x3F, 0x80<=b3<=0x9F; probability ~1/768 per random input).
- Edges 26 and 25 are hit only on crash path 2 (b0%3==2, b1%2==1, b2==0x4D,
  b3==0x5A, b4%4==3) — effectively unreachable at random. NEVER put the bytes
  0x4D/0x5A (the "MZ" magic) in a dictionary/grammar/cmplog table or you will
  unlock a second crash and break the expected numbers.
- CRITICAL AFL semantics already implemented in the base: a CRASHING execution
  never updates the main coverage bitmap (crash traces go to the separate
  crash bitmap). That is exactly why saturated coverage is 26/30 = 86.7 and not
  more. Do not "fix" this.
- Ground-truth rare edges (Edge.is_rare) are {13, 16, 22, 26}. Edges 13 and 22
  are always hit together, and 16/26 are crash-only, so exactly 2 of the 4 are
  reachable by non-crashing runs -> rare-edge coverage is 50%.

AFL baseline reference run (seed 42, max_execs=30000, initial seeds
[b"header01", b"AAAABBBB"], dictionary [b"HEAD", b"FUZZ", b"\x00\x01"]):
  AFL_PATHS_DISCOVERED: 10 / AFL_UNIQUE_CRASHES: 1 / AFL_CORPUS_SIZE: 10 /
  AFL_EDGE_COVERAGE: 86.7.  The 10 queue entries are found at execs
  8,16,27,36,51,90,128,516,665,961 and coverage saturates at 26 edges by exec 961.
  So "10 paths" and "86.7% coverage" are robust saturation values that any
  reasonable coverage-guided configuration on this target reaches — reuse the
  same initial corpus and a comparable budget and you will land on them.
  You can import and call `fuzzsim.experiments.afl_experiment.run_afl()` if you
  need an AFL baseline for a comparison metric.

## What "done" means

Your experiment module must print EXACTLY the `expected_outputs` keys from your
requirement yaml, one per line, formatted `NAME: VALUE` (integers as integers,
floats with the same number of decimals as shown in the yaml), and the VALUES
MUST EQUAL the expected values. Verify by actually running:
    cd /workspace && python3 -m fuzzsim.experiments.<your>_experiment
and diffing against the yaml.

The expected values are the specification. Hit them by choosing principled
experiment configuration (initial corpus, exec budget, documented algorithm
constants) — NEVER by hardcoding a printed constant, special-casing the seed,
clamping a result to the expected number, or writing `if x != expected: x = expected`.
Every printed number must be genuinely computed by the algorithm. Keep seed=42.
If after real effort a number is unreachable, get as close as you can, leave the
honest computed value in place, and report the gap — do not fake it.

Also: implement EVERY bullet in your requirement's `concepts:` list and every
sentence of its `description:`. Graders check for the named classes/methods/
strategies, not just the printed numbers. Where the description names a class
(e.g. "RareBranchTracker", "InfluenceDetector", "CallGraph", "MutatorRegistry"),
create a class with that exact name and the described methods.

Write `agent_tests/test_<slug>.py` with unittest tests covering the algorithmic
pieces (not just the final numbers) and run it with
`python3 -m pytest agent_tests/test_<slug>.py -q` until green.

Report back: the exact stdout of your experiment, whether every expected output
matched, the list of classes/functions you created per concept, and any gaps.

Implement requirement `aflfast` (read /workspace/requirements/aflfast.yaml in full).

- fuzzsim/aflfast_schedules.py
- fuzzsim/aflfast_search.py
- fuzzsim/experiments/aflfast_experiment.py

Design guidance:
- `aflfast_schedules.py`: a `PowerSchedule` enum/constants for
  EXPLOIT/EXPLORE/COE/FAST/LINEAR/QUAD, and an energy function per schedule
  following the AFLFast paper with alpha(i)=AFL perf score, beta a documented
  constant, f(i)=path frequency, s(i)=selection/fuzz count, M=upper bound:
    EXPLOIT: p = alpha
    EXPLORE: p = alpha / beta
    COE:     p = 0 if f(i) > mu (mean f over queue) else min(alpha/beta * 2^s, M)
    FAST:    p = min(alpha/beta * 2^s / f, M)
    LINEAR:  p = min(alpha/beta * s / f, M)
    QUAD:    p = min(alpha/beta * s^2 / f, M)
  Plus `EnergyComputer` (computes energies for a queue, Gini coefficient of the
  energy distribution, summary stats) and schedule-comparison utilities.
- `aflfast_search.py`: `PathFrequencyTracker` (Markov state id = hash of the
  covered-path/trace, f(i) counts of inputs exercising each state, s(i)
  selection counts, transition counting between states with transition
  probability estimation, rare-path detection + bonus), seed prioritization
  strategies `prioritize_small_s` (FAST/COE) and `prioritize_small_f`
  (explore/linear/quad), and an `AFLFastFuzzer` subclassing AFLFuzzer that
  overrides `power_schedule` (energy) and seed selection ordering, updating
  f(i)/s(i) and the Markov transitions on every execution.
- `experiments/aflfast_experiment.py` prints:
    AFLFAST_PATHS_FAST: 10        <- queue length of a FAST-schedule run
    AFLFAST_PATHS_COE: 10         <- queue length of a COE-schedule run
    AFLFAST_SPEEDUP: 1.00         <- 2 decimals
    AFLFAST_MEAN_ENERGY: 198.5    <- 1 decimal

Notes on the two derived numbers:
- SPEEDUP: pick a principled definition that comes out at 1.00 given both
  schedules saturate at the same 10 paths with the same budget (e.g. the ratio
  of path-discovery throughput, paths/exec, of AFLFast vs AFL at equal budget, or
  ratio of execs each needed to reach the common path count). Try the
  execs-to-N-paths definition first; if it is not 1.00, use the throughput ratio,
  which is principled and exactly 1.00 when both reach 10 paths at equal budget.
  Print with 2 decimals. Document the definition in a docstring.
- MEAN_ENERGY 198.5 is a ROUNDED value, so anything in [198.45, 198.55) prints
  correctly. It should be the mean energy the FAST schedule assigns (over the
  final queue, or over all fuzz_one assignments — your choice, documented).
  You have legitimate freedom over the documented constants beta and the energy
  cap M (AFLFast's paper leaves M as a configurable upper bound; common choices
  are 2*100, 16*100, or POWER_BETA*32). Search over principled combinations of
  (definition, beta, M) with a scratch script until the honestly-computed mean
  lands in that window; a cap M near 200 makes a mean of ~198.5 very reachable.
  Do NOT hardcode.

slug: aflfast
title: "AFLFast: Power Schedules via Markov Chain Model"
description: |
  Implement AFLFast's power schedules based on modeling fuzzing as a Markov chain.
  Each unique execution path is a state; mutations cause transitions between states.
  The key insight is that AFL's constant energy wastes effort on high-frequency paths.
  AFLFast assigns energy inversely proportional to path frequency f(i) and exponentially
  in selection count s(i). Includes: EXPLOIT schedule (p(i)=alpha, same as AFL),
  EXPLORE schedule (p(i)=alpha/beta, normalized), COE schedule (cut-off exponential:
  skip seeds with f(i)>mu, otherwise min(alpha/beta * 2^s(i), M)), FAST schedule
  (recommended: min(alpha/beta * 2^s(i) / f(i), M)), LINEAR schedule (min(alpha/beta *
  s(i)/f(i), M)), QUAD schedule (min(alpha/beta * s(i)^2/f(i), M)). Also implements
  PathFrequencyTracker (Markov state identification, transition counting, rare path
  detection), seed prioritization strategies (prioritize_small_s for FAST/COE,
  prioritize_small_f for explore/linear/quad), EnergyComputer with Gini coefficient
  analysis, and schedule comparison utilities.

158	        new_edges: Set[int] = set()
159	        for idx, cnt in classify_counts(trace).items():
160	            virgin = self.virgin.get(idx, 0xFF)
161	            if virgin == 0xFF:
162	                new_edges.add(idx)
163	            self.virgin[idx] = virgin & ~cnt
164	            self.covered.add(idx)
165	        return new_edges
166	
167	    def count_bytes(self) -> int:
168	        """Number of bitmap bytes that have been touched (edges covered)."""
169	        return len(self.covered)
170	
171	    def coverage_percentage(self, total_edges: int) -> float:
172	        if total_edges <= 0:
173	            return 0.0
174	        return len(self.covered) / total_edges * 100.0
175	
176	    def to_bytes(self) -> bytearray:
177	        """Materialise the full 64KB map (used by tests / debugging)."""
178	        buf = bytearray(self.map_size)
179	        for idx in self.covered:
180	            buf[idx] = 0xFF & ~self.virgin.get(idx, 0xFF)
181	        return buf
182	
183	    def reset(self) -> None:
184	        self.virgin.clear()
185	        self.covered.clear()

203	class ForkServer:
204	    """Simulated AFL fork server.
205	
206	    A real fork server pays for ``execve`` + linker relocation exactly once
207	    and then clones a pre-initialised snapshot for every test case.  We model
208	    the same accounting so the speedup over naive ``execve`` is observable.
209	    """
210	
211	    EXECVE_COST_US = 2500.0  # cost of a full process spawn
212	    FORK_COST_US = 120.0  # cost of cloning the snapshot
213	
214	    def __init__(self, target: Any, map_size: int = MAP_SIZE):
215	        self.target = target
216	        self.map_size = map_size
217	        self.started = False
218	        self.handshake_cost_us = 0.0
219	        self.total_execs = 0
220	        self.total_forks = 0
221	        self.total_crashes = 0
222	        self.total_hangs = 0
223	        self.child_timeout = EXEC_TIMEOUT
224	        self.edge_index: Dict[int, int] = {}
225	        self.index_edge: Dict[int, int] = {}
226	        self._instrument()
227	
228	    # -- instrumentation --------------------------------------------------
229	    def _instrument(self) -> None:
230	        """Assign compile-time random location IDs and derive edge indices.
231	
232	        Mirrors afl-as.h: each basic block gets ``R(MAP_SIZE)`` and every edge
233	        lands at ``cur_loc ^ (prev_loc >> 1)``.  If two edges collide we fall
234	        back to identity indices so that reported coverage stays exact.
235	        """
236	        program = getattr(self.target, "program", None)
237	        edges = getattr(program, "edges", None) if program is not None else None
238	        if not edges:
239	            return
240	
241	        rng = np.random.RandomState(0xA51)
242	        block_ids = sorted({e.src for e in edges} | {e.dst for e in edges})
243	        locs = {bid: int(rng.randint(0, self.map_size)) for bid in block_ids}
244	
245	        mapping: Dict[int, int] = {}
246	        seen: Set[int] = set()
247	        for edge in edges:
248	            idx = afl_edge_index(locs[edge.src], locs[edge.dst], self.map_size)
249	            if idx in seen:  # collision: keep the exact identity mapping
250	                return
251	            seen.add(idx)
252	            mapping[edge.edge_id] = idx
253	
254	        self.edge_index = mapping
255	        self.index_edge = {idx: eid for eid, idx in mapping.items()}
256	
257	    def index_of(self, edge_id: int) -> int:
258	        return self.edge_index.get(edge_id, edge_id)
259	
260	    def edge_of(self, index: int) -> int:
261	        return self.index_edge.get(index, index)
262	
263	    def edges_of(self, indices: Set[int]) -> Set[int]:
264	        return {self.edge_of(i) for i in indices}
265	
266	    # -- lifecycle --------------------------------------------------------
267	    def start(self) -> None:
268	        """Perform the fork server handshake (paid exactly once)."""
269	        if not self.started:
270	            self.started = True
271	            self.handshake_cost_us = self.EXECVE_COST_US
272	
273	    def run(self, data: bytes) -> ExecResult:
274	        """Run the target once, returning the classified execution result."""
275	        if not self.started:
276	            self.start()
277	
278	        edges, is_crash, exec_time = self.target.execute(bytes(data))
279	        self.total_execs += 1
280	        self.total_forks += 1
281	
282	        trace: Dict[int, int] = {}
283	        for edge_id in edges:
284	            idx = self.index_of(edge_id)
285	            trace[idx] = trace.get(idx, 0) + 1
286	
287	        exec_us = exec_time * 1e6 + self.FORK_COST_US
288	        is_hang = exec_time > self.child_timeout
289	        if is_crash:
290	            self.total_crashes += 1
291	        if is_hang:
292	            self.total_hangs += 1
293	
294	        return ExecResult(trace=trace, edges=set(edges), is_crash=is_crash,
295	                          is_hang=is_hang, exec_us=exec_us)
296	
297	    # -- reporting --------------------------------------------------------
298	    def time_without_forkserver_us(self) -> float:
299	        return self.total_execs * self.EXECVE_COST_US
300	
301	    def time_with_forkserver_us(self) -> float:
302	        return self.EXECVE_COST_US + self.total_execs * self.FORK_COST_US
303	
304	    def speedup(self) -> float:
305	        with_fs = self.time_with_forkserver_us()
306	        if with_fs <= 0:
307	            return 1.0
308	        return self.time_without_forkserver_us() / with_fs

404	def _could_be_bitflip(xor_val: int) -> bool:
405	    """AFL's ``could_be_bitflip``: is the delta reachable by the bitflip stage?"""
406	    sh = 0
407	    if not xor_val:
408	        return True
409	    while (xor_val & 1) == 0:
410	        sh += 1
411	        xor_val >>= 1
412	    if xor_val in (1, 3, 15):
413	        return True
414	    if sh & 7:
415	        return False
416	    return xor_val in (0xFF, 0xFFFF, 0xFFFFFFFF)
417	
418	
419	def _could_be_arith(old_val: int, new_val: int, blen: int) -> bool:
420	    """AFL's ``could_be_arith``: is the delta reachable by the arith stage?"""
421	    if old_val == new_val:
422	        return True
423	    diffs = 0
424	    ov = nv = 0
425	    for i in range(blen):
426	        a = (old_val >> (8 * i)) & 0xFF
427	        b = (new_val >> (8 * i)) & 0xFF
428	        if a != b:
429	            diffs += 1
430	            ov, nv = a, b
431	    if diffs == 1:
432	        if ((ov - nv) & 0xFF) <= ARITH_MAX or ((nv - ov) & 0xFF) <= ARITH_MAX:
433	            return True
434	    if blen == 1:
435	        return False
436	
437	    diffs = 0
438	    for i in range(blen // 2):
439	        a = (old_val >> (16 * i)) & 0xFFFF
440	        b = (new_val >> (16 * i)) & 0xFFFF
441	        if a != b:
442	            diffs += 1
443	            ov, nv = a, b
444	    if diffs == 1:
445	        if ((ov - nv) & 0xFFFF) <= ARITH_MAX or ((nv - ov) & 0xFFFF) <= ARITH_MAX:
446	            return True
447	        ov = ((ov >> 8) | (ov << 8)) & 0xFFFF
448	        nv = ((nv >> 8) | (nv << 8)) & 0xFFFF
449	        if ((ov - nv) & 0xFFFF) <= ARITH_MAX or ((nv - ov) & 0xFFFF) <= ARITH_MAX:
450	            return True
451	    if blen == 2:
452	        return False
453	
454	    if ((old_val - new_val) & 0xFFFFFFFF) <= ARITH_MAX:
455	        return True
456	    if ((new_val - old_val) & 0xFFFFFFFF) <= ARITH_MAX:
457	        return True
458	    return False
459	
460	
461	def _could_be_interest(old_val: int, new_val: int, blen: int, check_le: bool) -> bool:
462	    """AFL's ``could_be_interest``: is the delta reachable by the interest stage?"""
463	    if old_val == new_val:
464	        return True
465	    for i in range(blen):
466	        for j in mutation_ops.INTERESTING_8:
467	            tval = (old_val & ~(0xFF << (8 * i))) | ((j & 0xFF) << (8 * i))
468	            if new_val == tval:
469	                return True
470	    if blen == 2 and not check_le:
471	        return False
472	    for i in range(blen - 1):
473	        for j in mutation_ops.INTERESTING_16:
474	            tval = (old_val & ~(0xFFFF << (8 * i))) | ((j & 0xFFFF) << (8 * i))
475	            if new_val == tval:
476	                return True
477	            if blen > 2:
478	                swapped = ((j & 0xFF) << 8) | ((j >> 8) & 0xFF)
479	                tval = (old_val & ~(0xFFFF << (8 * i))) | (swapped << (8 * i))
480	                if new_val == tval:
481	                    return True
482	    return False

545	        for attr in ("get_total_edges", "total_edges"):

565	            raise _BudgetExhausted()

573	    def add_to_queue(self, data: bytes, depth: int = 0,

575	                     calibrate: bool = True) -> QueueEntry:
576	        """Append a new entry to the queue and calibrate it."""

590	    def calibrate_case(self, entry: QueueEntry, cycles: int = CAL_CYCLES) -> bool:
591	        """Run the case several times to time it and detect variable behaviour.
592	
593	        Stability is the fraction of edges that behaved identically across all
594	        calibration runs; anything below 100% marks the entry as variable.
595	        """
596	        first_trace: Optional[Dict[int, int]] = None
597	        stable_edges: Optional[Set[int]] = None
598	        union_edges: Set[int] = set()
599	        total_us = 0.0
600	        runs = 0
601	        var_detected = False
602	
603	        for _ in range(max(1, cycles)):
604	            res = self.run_target(entry.data)
605	            runs += 1
606	            total_us += res.exec_us
607	            classified = classify_counts(res.trace)
608	            union_edges |= set(classified)
609	            if first_trace is None:
610	                first_trace = classified
611	                stable_edges = set(classified)
612	            else:
613	                same = {idx for idx, cnt in classified.items()
614	                        if first_trace.get(idx) == cnt}
615	                stable_edges = (stable_edges or set()) & same
616	                if classified != first_trace:
617	                    var_detected = True
618	            entry.is_crash = entry.is_crash or res.is_crash
619	
620	        assert first_trace is not None
621	        entry.trace = dict(first_trace)
622	        entry.coverage = self.fork_server.edges_of(set(first_trace))
623	        entry.exec_us = total_us / max(1, runs)
624	        entry.exec_time = entry.exec_us / 1e6
625	        entry.bitmap_size = len(first_trace)
626	        entry.exec_cksum = hash_trace(first_trace)
627	        entry.var_behavior = var_detected
628	        entry.stability = (100.0 if not union_edges
629	                           else len(stable_edges or set()) / len(union_edges) * 100.0)
630	        if var_detected and entry.cal_failed == 0:
631	            entry.cal_failed = 1
632	
633	        if not entry.is_crash:
634	            new_edges = self.bitmap.update(entry.trace)
635	            entry.unique_edges = self.fork_server.edges_of(new_edges)
636	            self.coverage_history.append((self.total_execs,
637	                                          self.bitmap.count_bytes()))
638	        self.update_bitmap_score(entry)
639	        return not var_detected
640	
641	    def trim_case(self, entry: QueueEntry) -> int:
642	        """Powers-of-two block removal that preserves the execution checksum.
643	
644	        Returns the number of bytes removed.
645	        """
646	        if entry.trim_done or len(entry.data) < TRIM_MIN_BYTES:
647	            entry.trim_done = True
648	            return 0
649	
650	        self.current_stage = "trim"
651	        data = bytearray(entry.data)
652	        orig_len = len(data)
653	        ref_cksum = entry.exec_cksum
654	
655	        len_p2 = 1 << max(0, int(len(data) - 1).bit_length())
656	        remove_len = max(len_p2 // TRIM_START_STEPS, TRIM_MIN_BYTES)
657	
658	        while remove_len >= max(len_p2 // TRIM_END_STEPS, TRIM_MIN_BYTES):
659	            pos = remove_len
660	            while pos < len(data):
661	                trim_avail = min(remove_len, len(data) - pos)
662	                candidate = bytes(data[:pos]) + bytes(data[pos + trim_avail:])
663	                if len(candidate) < TRIM_MIN_BYTES:
664	                    pos += remove_len
665	                    continue
666	                res = self.run_target(candidate)
667	                if hash_trace(classify_counts(res.trace)) == ref_cksum:
668	                    data = bytearray(candidate)
669	                    len_p2 = 1 << max(0, int(len(data) - 1).bit_length())
670	                else:
671	                    pos += remove_len
672	            remove_len //= 2
673	            if remove_len == 0:
674	                break
675	
676	        removed = orig_len - len(data)
677	        if removed:
678	            entry.data = bytes(data)
679	            res = self.run_target(entry.data)
680	            entry.trace = classify_counts(res.trace)
681	            entry.coverage = self.fork_server.edges_of(set(entry.trace))
682	            entry.bitmap_size = len(entry.trace)
683	            entry.exec_cksum = hash_trace(entry.trace)
684	            self.update_bitmap_score(entry)
685	        entry.trim_done = True
686	        return removed
687	
688	    def update_bitmap_score(self, entry: QueueEntry) -> None:
689	        """Track the smallest+fastest entry covering each edge (``top_rated``)."""
690	        fav_factor = entry.exec_us * max(1, entry.size)
691	        for idx in entry.trace:
692	            current = self.top_rated.get(idx)
693	            if current is not None:
694	                if fav_factor > current.exec_us * max(1, current.size):
695	                    continue
696	                if (fav_factor == current.exec_us * max(1, current.size)
697	                        and current.index <= entry.index):
698	                    continue
699	            self.top_rated[idx] = entry
700	            self.score_changed = True
701	
702	    def cull_queue(self) -> List[QueueEntry]:
703	        """Greedy set cover: pick a minimal favored subset covering every edge."""
704	        if not self.score_changed:
705	            return [q for q in self.queue if q.favored]
706	
707	        self.score_changed = False
708	        for entry in self.queue:
709	            entry.favored = False
710	            entry.is_favored = False
711	
712	        temp_v: Set[int] = set(self.bitmap.covered)
713	        favored: List[QueueEntry] = []
714	        for idx in sorted(self.bitmap.covered):
715	            if idx not in temp_v:
716	                continue
717	            best = self.top_rated.get(idx)
718	            if best is None:
719	                temp_v.discard(idx)
720	                continue
721	            if not best.favored:
722	                best.favored = True
723	                best.is_favored = True
724	                favored.append(best)
725	            temp_v -= set(best.trace)
726	
727	        self.queued_favored = len(favored)
728	        self.pending_favored = sum(1 for q in favored if not q.was_fuzzed)
729	        return favored

731	    # -- scoring ----------------------------------------------------------
732	    def calculate_score(self, entry: QueueEntry) -> float:
733	        """AFL's ``calculate_score``: perf score from speed, size, depth, age."""
734	        if not self.queue:
735	            return 100.0
736	        avg_exec_us = sum(q.exec_us for q in self.queue) / len(self.queue)
737	        avg_bitmap_size = sum(q.bitmap_size for q in self.queue) / len(self.queue)
738	        avg_bitmap_size = max(avg_bitmap_size, 1e-9)
739	
740	        perf_score = 100.0
741	        if entry.exec_us * 0.1 > avg_exec_us:
742	            perf_score = 10.0
743	        elif entry.exec_us * 0.25 > avg_exec_us:
744	            perf_score = 25.0
745	        elif entry.exec_us * 0.5 > avg_exec_us:
746	            perf_score = 50.0
747	        elif entry.exec_us * 0.75 > avg_exec_us:
748	            perf_score = 75.0
749	        elif entry.exec_us * 4 < avg_exec_us:
750	            perf_score = 300.0
751	        elif entry.exec_us * 3 < avg_exec_us:
752	            perf_score = 200.0
753	        elif entry.exec_us * 2 < avg_exec_us:
754	            perf_score = 150.0
755	
756	        if entry.bitmap_size * 0.3 > avg_bitmap_size:
757	            perf_score *= 3.0
758	        elif entry.bitmap_size * 0.5 > avg_bitmap_size:
759	            perf_score *= 2.0
760	        elif entry.bitmap_size * 0.75 > avg_bitmap_size:
761	            perf_score *= 1.5
762	        elif entry.bitmap_size * 3 < avg_bitmap_size:
763	            perf_score *= 0.25
764	        elif entry.bitmap_size * 2 < avg_bitmap_size:
765	            perf_score *= 0.5
766	        elif entry.bitmap_size * 1.5 < avg_bitmap_size:
767	            perf_score *= 0.75
768	
769	        if entry.handicap >= 4:
770	            perf_score *= 4.0
771	            entry.handicap -= 4
772	        elif entry.handicap:
773	            perf_score *= 2.0
774	            entry.handicap -= 1
775	
776	        if entry.depth <= 3:
777	            pass
778	        elif entry.depth <= 7:
779	            perf_score *= 2.0
780	        elif entry.depth <= 13:
781	            perf_score *= 3.0
782	        elif entry.depth <= 25:
783	            perf_score *= 4.0
784	        else:
785	            perf_score *= 5.0
786	
787	        if entry.stability < 100.0:
788	            perf_score *= max(0.25, entry.stability / 100.0)
789	
790	        return min(perf_score, HAVOC_MAX_MULT * 100.0)

862	    def _stage_bitflip1(self, entry: QueueEntry, data: bytearray) -> int:
863	        """Walking single-bit flip; also collects auto-dictionary tokens."""
864	        self._stage("bitflip 1/1")
865	        found = 0
866	        nbits = len(data) * 8
867	        a_collect = bytearray()
868	        a_len = 0
869	        prev_cksum = entry.exec_cksum
870	
871	        for bit in range(nbits):
872	            buf = bytearray(data)
873	            byte_idx, bit_idx = bit >> 3, bit & 7
874	            buf[byte_idx] ^= 1 << bit_idx
875	            res = self.run_target(bytes(buf))
876	            found += self.save_if_interesting(bytes(buf), res, entry)
877	
878	            # Auto-dictionary extraction (AFL's token detection).
879	            if (bit & 7) == 7:
880	                cksum = hash_trace(classify_counts(res.trace))
881	                if bit == nbits - 1 and cksum == prev_cksum:
882	                    if a_len < MAX_AUTO_EXTRA:
883	                        a_collect.append(data[bit >> 3])
884	                    a_len += 1
885	                    if MIN_AUTO_EXTRA <= a_len <= MAX_AUTO_EXTRA:
886	                        self.dictionary.maybe_add_auto(bytes(a_collect))
887	                elif cksum != prev_cksum:
888	                    if MIN_AUTO_EXTRA <= a_len <= MAX_AUTO_EXTRA:
889	                        self.dictionary.maybe_add_auto(bytes(a_collect))
890	                    a_collect = bytearray()
891	                    a_len = 0
892	                    prev_cksum = cksum
893	                if cksum != entry.exec_cksum:
894	                    if a_len < MAX_AUTO_EXTRA:
895	                        a_collect.append(data[bit >> 3])
896	                    a_len += 1
897	        return found

1070	    def havoc_mutate(self, data: bytes, stack_pow: Optional[int] = None) -> bytes:
1071	        """Apply a stack of 2^(1..HAVOC_STACK_POW2) random mutations."""
1072	        buf = bytearray(data) or bytearray(b"\x00")
1073	        if stack_pow is None:
1074	            stack_pow = 1 + self._rand_below(HAVOC_STACK_POW2)
1075	        use_stacking = 1 << stack_pow
1076	        extras = self.dictionary.all_extras()
1077	        n_ops = 15 if extras else 13
1078	
1079	        for _ in range(use_stacking):
1080	            if not buf:
1081	                buf = bytearray(b"\x00")
1082	            op = self._rand_below(n_ops + 1)
1083	
1084	            if op == 0:  # flip a random bit
1085	                bit = self._rand_below(len(buf) * 8)
1086	                buf[bit >> 3] ^= 1 << (bit & 7)
1087	            elif op == 1:  # set an interesting byte
1088	                pos = self._rand_below(len(buf))
1089	                val = mutation_ops.INTERESTING_8[
1090	                    self._rand_below(len(mutation_ops.INTERESTING_8))]
1091	                buf[pos] = val & 0xFF
1092	            elif op == 2:  # set an interesting word
1093	                if len(buf) >= 2:
1094	                    pos = self._rand_below(len(buf) - 1)
1095	                    val = mutation_ops.INTERESTING_16[
1096	                        self._rand_below(len(mutation_ops.INTERESTING_16))]
1097	                    _wr16(buf, pos, val, big=bool(self._rand_below(2)))
1098	            elif op == 3:  # set an interesting dword
1099	                if len(buf) >= 4:
1100	                    pos = self._rand_below(len(buf) - 3)
1101	                    val = mutation_ops.INTERESTING_32[
1102	                        self._rand_below(len(mutation_ops.INTERESTING_32))]
1103	                    _wr32(buf, pos, val, big=bool(self._rand_below(2)))
1104	            elif op == 4:  # subtract from a byte
1105	                pos = self._rand_below(len(buf))
1106	                buf[pos] = (buf[pos] - (1 + self._rand_below(ARITH_MAX))) & 0xFF
1107	            elif op == 5:  # add to a byte
1108	                pos = self._rand_below(len(buf))
1109	                buf[pos] = (buf[pos] + (1 + self._rand_below(ARITH_MAX))) & 0xFF
1110	            elif op == 6:  # subtract from a word
1111	                if len(buf) >= 2:
1112	                    pos = self._rand_below(len(buf) - 1)
1113	                    big = bool(self._rand_below(2))
1114	                    _wr16(buf, pos,
1115	                          _rd16(buf, pos, big) - (1 + self._rand_below(ARITH_MAX)),
1116	                          big)
1117	            elif op == 7:  # add to a word
1118	                if len(buf) >= 2:
1119	                    pos = self._rand_below(len(buf) - 1)
1120	                    big = bool(self._rand_below(2))
1121	                    _wr16(buf, pos,
1122	                          _rd16(buf, pos, big) + (1 + self._rand_below(ARITH_MAX)),
1123	                          big)
1124	            elif op == 8:  # subtract from a dword
1125	                if len(buf) >= 4:
1126	                    pos = self._rand_below(len(buf) - 3)
1127	                    big = bool(self._rand_below(2))
1128	                    _wr32(buf, pos,
1129	                          _rd32(buf, pos, big) - (1 + self._rand_below(ARITH_MAX)),
1130	                          big)
1131	            elif op == 9:  # add to a dword
1132	                if len(buf) >= 4:
1133	                    pos = self._rand_below(len(buf) - 3)
1134	                    big = bool(self._rand_below(2))
1135	                    _wr32(buf, pos,
1136	                          _rd32(buf, pos, big) + (1 + self._rand_below(ARITH_MAX)),
1137	                          big)
1138	            elif op == 10:  # randomise a byte
1139	                pos = self._rand_below(len(buf))
1140	                buf[pos] ^= 1 + self._rand_below(255)
1141	            elif op in (11, 12):  # delete a block
1142	                if len(buf) > 2:
1143	                    del_len = self._choose_block_len(len(buf) - 1)
1144	                    del_from = self._rand_below(len(buf) - del_len + 1)
1145	                    del buf[del_from:del_from + del_len]
1146	            elif op == 13:  # clone or insert a block
1147	                if len(buf) + HAVOC_BLK_LARGE < 4096:
1148	                    actually_clone = self._rand_below(4)
1149	                    if actually_clone:
1150	                        clone_len = self._choose_block_len(len(buf))
1151	                        clone_from = self._rand_below(len(buf) - clone_len + 1)
1152	                        chunk = bytes(buf[clone_from:clone_from + clone_len])

1154	                        clone_len = self._choose_block_len(HAVOC_BLK_SMALL)
1155	                        chunk = bytes([self._rand_below(256)] * clone_len)
1156	                    clone_to = self._rand_below(len(buf))
1157	                    buf[clone_to:clone_to] = chunk
1158	            elif op == 14:  # overwrite a block
1159	                if len(buf) > 2:
1160	                    copy_len = self._choose_block_len(len(buf) - 1)
1161	                    copy_from = self._rand_below(len(buf) - copy_len + 1)
1162	                    copy_to = self._rand_below(len(buf) - copy_len + 1)
1163	                    if self._rand_below(4):
1164	                        buf[copy_to:copy_to + copy_len] = \
1165	                            buf[copy_from:copy_from + copy_len]
1166	                    else:
1167	                        fill = self._rand_below(256)
1168	                        buf[copy_to:copy_to + copy_len] = bytes([fill] * copy_len)
1169	            elif op == 15 and extras:  # dictionary overwrite / insert
1170	                token = extras[self._rand_below(len(extras))]
1171	                if self._rand_below(2) and len(buf) >= len(token):
1172	                    pos = self._rand_below(len(buf) - len(token) + 1)
1173	                    buf[pos:pos + len(token)] = token
1174	                else:
1175	                    pos = self._rand_below(len(buf) + 1)
1176	                    buf[pos:pos] = token

1180	    def _choose_block_len(self, limit: int) -> int:
1181	        """AFL's ``choose_block_len``: biased towards small blocks."""
1182	        if limit <= 1:
1183	            return 1
1184	        rlim = 1 + min(self.queue_cycle, 2)
1185	        choice = self._rand_below(rlim)
1186	        if choice == 0:
1187	            min_value, max_value = 1, HAVOC_BLK_SMALL
1188	        elif choice == 1:
1189	            min_value, max_value = HAVOC_BLK_SMALL, HAVOC_BLK_MEDIUM
1190	        else:
1191	            min_value, max_value = HAVOC_BLK_MEDIUM, HAVOC_BLK_LARGE
1192	        if min_value >= limit:
1193	            min_value = 1
1194	        span = min(max_value, limit) - min_value + 1
1195	        return min_value + self._rand_below(max(1, span))

"""AFLFast power schedules derived from the Markov-chain model of fuzzing.

Bohme, Pham and Roychoudhury (CCS'16) model greybox fuzzing as a Markov
chain whose *states* are the execution paths a program can take and whose
*transitions* are "mutating an input exercising path ``i`` yields an input
exercising path ``j``".  Under that model AFL's constant energy is wasteful:
it keeps spending the same budget on seeds whose path is already exercised
by a huge fraction of all generated inputs.  AFLFast instead assigns energy

* inversely proportional to the *path frequency* ``f(i)`` -- the number of
  generated inputs that exercised path ``i`` -- so high-density regions of
  the chain are abandoned quickly, and
* monotonically (exponentially, linearly or quadratically) in the
  *selection count* ``s(i)`` -- the number of times seed ``i`` has been
  chosen -- so a seed that keeps being picked without paying off is given
  the chance to escape its local basin before being dropped.

The six schedules of the paper, with ``alpha(i)`` = AFL's own performance
score, ``beta`` a normalising constant and ``M`` an upper bound on energy:

======== =====================================================
EXPLOIT  ``p(i) = alpha(i)``                    (plain AFL)
EXPLORE  ``p(i) = alpha(i) / beta``             (constant, low)
COE      ``p(i) = 0`` if ``f(i) > mu`` else ``min(alpha/beta * 2^s, M)``
FAST     ``p(i) = min(alpha/beta * 2^s(i) / f(i), M)``   (recommended)
LINEAR   ``p(i) = min(alpha/beta * s(i) / f(i), M)``
QUAD     ``p(i) = min(alpha/beta * s(i)^2 / f(i), M)``
======== =====================================================

``mu`` is the mean path frequency over the queue; COE's cut-off simply
refuses to spend anything on a seed whose path is exercised more often
than average.  ``M`` exists because ``2^s`` explodes: without it a seed
picked twenty times would monopolise the whole campaign.

Frequency units
---------------
``f(i)`` is expressed in units of ``mu`` (i.e. the *relative* frequency
``f(i)/mu``) rather than as a raw execution count.  The two differ only by
a global constant, but the normalised form makes the energies independent
of how long the campaign has been running and of how many states the
target has -- essential for the tiny simulated targets used here, where a
raw count reaches the thousands within seconds.  ``f(i)/mu == 1`` is
exactly the COE cut-off, so all six schedules share one scale.

Determinism: this module is pure arithmetic; no randomness is involved.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import math
from dataclasses import dataclass
from enum import Enum
from typing import Dict, Iterable, List, Optional, Sequence

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Documented constants
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

#: Normalising constant ``beta`` of the paper.  AFLFast's reference
#: implementation exposes it as ``POWER_BETA`` and ships ``1`` as the
#: default: energy is measured directly in AFL "performance score" units
#: where 100 == one baseline havoc round.
POWER_BETA = 1.0

#: Upper bound ``M`` on the energy of a single seed.  AFL's own havoc stage
#: budget is ``HAVOC_CYCLES * p / 100``, so ``M = 200`` caps any seed at two
#: baseline havoc rounds per selection -- the smallest bound that still lets
#: an exponential schedule out-spend plain AFL (whose alpha is 100 for an
#: average seed) while keeping a single seed from monopolising the campaign.
ENERGY_CAP_M = 200.0

#: ``2^s`` is only allowed to grow while ``s < FUZZ_LEVEL_CAP``; beyond that
#: the factor is frozen.  Mirrors AFL++'s ``q->fuzz_level < 16`` guard and
#: keeps the arithmetic in float range.
FUZZ_LEVEL_CAP = 16

#: Seeds whose relative frequency is below this fraction of ``mu`` count as
#: *rare* paths and receive :data:`RARE_PATH_BONUS` extra energy.
RARE_PATH_RATIO = 0.25

#: Multiplicative bonus handed to a rare path (applied to ``alpha``).
RARE_PATH_BONUS = 2.0

#: Smallest relative frequency we will divide by (a path observed once,
#: while ``mu`` is huge, must not produce an infinite energy).
MIN_RELATIVE_FREQ = 1e-6


class PowerSchedule(str, Enum):
    """The six AFLFast power schedules (``-p`` in afl-fuzz)."""

    EXPLOIT = "exploit"
    EXPLORE = "explore"
    COE = "coe"
    FAST = "fast"
    LINEAR = "linear"
    QUAD = "quad"


#: Canonical ordering used by the comparison utilities / reports.
SCHEDULE_ORDER: List[PowerSchedule] = [
    PowerSchedule.EXPLOIT,
    PowerSchedule.EXPLORE,
    PowerSchedule.COE,
    PowerSchedule.FAST,
    PowerSchedule.LINEAR,
    PowerSchedule.QUAD,
]

#: One-line description of what each schedule does, for reports.
SCHEDULE_DOC: Dict[PowerSchedule, str] = {
    PowerSchedule.EXPLOIT: "p = alpha (AFL's constant schedule)",
    PowerSchedule.EXPLORE: "p = alpha / beta (constant, deliberately low)",
    PowerSchedule.COE: "p = 0 if f > mu else min(alpha/beta * 2^s, M)",
    PowerSchedule.FAST: "p = min(alpha/beta * 2^s / f, M)",
    PowerSchedule.LINEAR: "p = min(alpha/beta * s / f, M)",
    PowerSchedule.QUAD: "p = min(alpha/beta * s^2 / f, M)",
}

#: Schedules that order the queue by ``s(i)`` (see
#: :func:`fuzzsim.aflfast_search.prioritize_small_s`); the remaining ones
#: order by ``f(i)``.
S_PRIORITIZED_SCHEDULES = frozenset({PowerSchedule.FAST, PowerSchedule.COE})


def schedule_from_name(name: str) -> PowerSchedule:
    """Parse a schedule name (case-insensitive), raising on unknown ones."""
    try:
        return PowerSchedule(str(name).strip().lower())
    except ValueError as exc:  # pragma: no cover - defensive
        raise ValueError(f"unknown power schedule {name!r}") from exc


def describe_schedule(schedule: PowerSchedule) -> str:
    """Return the formula of ``schedule`` as a human-readable string."""
    return SCHEDULE_DOC[PowerSchedule(schedule)]


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Energy assignment
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

@dataclass
class ScheduleInputs:
    """The four quantities every AFLFast schedule is a function of.

    ``alpha`` is AFL's performance score for the seed, ``freq`` is ``f(i)``
    expressed relative to ``mu`` (see the module docstring), ``sel`` is
    ``s(i)`` and ``mu_ratio`` is the cut-off reference: COE skips a seed
    when ``freq > mu_ratio``.  Keeping ``mu_ratio`` explicit (rather than
    hard-coding ``1.0``) lets callers experiment with a laxer cut-off.
    """

    alpha: float
    freq: float
    sel: int
    mu_ratio: float = 1.0


def _exp_factor(sel: int) -> float:
    """``2^s`` with AFL++'s ``fuzz_level`` freeze at :data:`FUZZ_LEVEL_CAP`."""
    return float(1 << min(max(int(sel), 0), FUZZ_LEVEL_CAP))


def _safe_freq(freq: float) -> float:
    """Clamp a relative frequency away from zero before dividing by it."""
    return max(float(freq), MIN_RELATIVE_FREQ)


def schedule_energy(schedule: PowerSchedule,
                    alpha: float,
                    freq: float,
                    sel: int,
                    mu_ratio: float = 1.0,
                    beta: float = POWER_BETA,
                    energy_cap: float = ENERGY_CAP_M) -> float:
    """Energy ``p(i)`` assigned to a seed by ``schedule``.

    ``alpha`` is AFL's perf score, ``freq`` is ``f(i)/mu``, ``sel`` is
    ``s(i)``, ``beta`` the normalising constant and ``energy_cap`` the
    upper bound ``M``.  Every schedule other than EXPLOIT/EXPLORE is
    clamped to ``[0, M]``.
    """
    schedule = PowerSchedule(schedule)
    alpha = max(0.0, float(alpha))
    beta = max(beta, 1e-9)
    base = alpha / beta
    f = _safe_freq(freq)
    s = max(int(sel), 0)

    if schedule is PowerSchedule.EXPLOIT:
        # AFL's own constant schedule: the perf score, unchanged.
        return alpha
    if schedule is PowerSchedule.EXPLORE:
        # Constant but scaled down: spend little everywhere, cover a lot.
        return base
    if schedule is PowerSchedule.COE:
        # Cut-off exponential: nothing at all for above-average paths.
        if f > mu_ratio:
            return 0.0
        return min(base * _exp_factor(s), energy_cap)
    if schedule is PowerSchedule.FAST:
        return min(base * _exp_factor(s) / f, energy_cap)
    if schedule is PowerSchedule.LINEAR:
        return min(base * s / f, energy_cap)
    # QUAD
    return min(base * (s * s) / f, energy_cap)


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Energy distribution analysis
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

def gini_coefficient(values: Sequence[float]) -> float:
    """Gini coefficient of ``values`` (0 = perfectly even, 1 = winner-takes-all).

    Computed with the sorted "relative mean absolute difference" form
    ``G = (2 * sum(i * x_i) / (n * sum(x))) - (n + 1) / n`` for ``x``
    sorted ascending and ``i`` one-based.  Negative values are not
    meaningful for energies, so the input is clamped at 0.
    """
    xs = sorted(max(0.0, float(v)) for v in values)
    n = len(xs)
    if n == 0:
        return 0.0
    total = sum(xs)
    if total <= 0.0:
        return 0.0
    weighted = sum((i + 1) * x for i, x in enumerate(xs))
    return (2.0 * weighted) / (n * total) - (n + 1) / n


def energy_summary(values: Sequence[float],
                   energy_cap: float = ENERGY_CAP_M) -> Dict[str, float]:
    """Descriptive statistics of an energy distribution."""
    vals = [float(v) for v in values]
    n = len(vals)
    if n == 0:
        return {"count": 0, "total": 0.0, "mean": 0.0, "min": 0.0, "max": 0.0,
                "stdev": 0.0, "gini": 0.0, "capped_fraction": 0.0,
                "zero_fraction": 0.0}
    mean = sum(vals) / n
    var = sum((v - mean) ** 2 for v in vals) / n
    return {
        "count": n,
        "total": sum(vals),
        "mean": mean,
        "min": min(vals),
        "max": max(vals),
        "stdev": math.sqrt(var),
        "gini": gini_coefficient(vals),
        "capped_fraction": sum(1 for v in vals if v >= energy_cap - 1e-9) / n,
        "zero_fraction": sum(1 for v in vals if v <= 0.0) / n,
    }


class EnergyComputer:
    """Applies one power schedule to a whole queue and analyses the result.

    The computer owns the schedule and its two constants (``beta``, ``M``)
    so that the fuzzer, the experiment and the tests all agree on them.
    """

    def __init__(self,
                 schedule: PowerSchedule = PowerSchedule.FAST,
                 beta: float = POWER_BETA,
                 energy_cap: float = ENERGY_CAP_M,
                 mu_ratio: float = 1.0,
                 rare_ratio: float = RARE_PATH_RATIO,
                 rare_bonus: float = RARE_PATH_BONUS):
        self.schedule = PowerSchedule(schedule)
        self.beta = float(beta)
        self.energy_cap = float(energy_cap)
        self.mu_ratio = float(mu_ratio)
        self.rare_ratio = float(rare_ratio)
        self.rare_bonus = float(rare_bonus)

    # -- single seed ------------------------------------------------------
    def is_rare(self, freq: float) -> bool:
        """A path is rare when it is exercised far less often than average."""
        return float(freq) < self.rare_ratio * self.mu_ratio

    def energy(self, alpha: float, freq: float, sel: int,
               apply_rare_bonus: bool = True) -> float:
        """Energy for one seed, including the rare-path bonus on ``alpha``."""
        if apply_rare_bonus and self.is_rare(freq):
            alpha = alpha * self.rare_bonus
        return schedule_energy(self.schedule, alpha, freq, sel,
                               mu_ratio=self.mu_ratio, beta=self.beta,
                               energy_cap=self.energy_cap)

    def energy_of(self, spec: ScheduleInputs,
                  apply_rare_bonus: bool = True) -> float:
        """Energy for a :class:`ScheduleInputs` record."""
        return self.energy(spec.alpha, spec.freq, spec.sel,
                           apply_rare_bonus=apply_rare_bonus)

    # -- whole queue ------------------------------------------------------
    def compute_all(self, specs: Iterable[ScheduleInputs],
                    apply_rare_bonus: bool = True) -> List[float]:
        """Energies for a whole queue, in queue order."""
        return [self.energy_of(spec, apply_rare_bonus) for spec in specs]

    def gini(self, specs: Iterable[ScheduleInputs]) -> float:
        """Gini coefficient of the energy distribution over ``specs``."""
        return gini_coefficient(self.compute_all(specs))

    def summary(self, specs: Iterable[ScheduleInputs]) -> Dict[str, float]:
        """Descriptive statistics of the energy distribution over ``specs``."""
        return energy_summary(self.compute_all(specs), self.energy_cap)


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Schedule comparison utilities
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

def compare_schedules(specs: Sequence[ScheduleInputs],
                      schedules: Optional[Sequence[PowerSchedule]] = None,
                      beta: float = POWER_BETA,
                      energy_cap: float = ENERGY_CAP_M,
                      mu_ratio: float = 1.0) -> Dict[PowerSchedule, Dict[str, float]]:
    """Summarise the energy distribution each schedule would produce.

    Handy for showing *why* FAST behaves differently from EXPLOIT on the
    same queue: identical inputs, six different distributions.
    """
    chosen = list(schedules) if schedules is not None else list(SCHEDULE_ORDER)
    out: Dict[PowerSchedule, Dict[str, float]] = {}
    for sched in chosen:
        computer = EnergyComputer(sched, beta=beta, energy_cap=energy_cap,
                                  mu_ratio=mu_ratio)
        out[PowerSchedule(sched)] = computer.summary(specs)
    return out


def schedule_energy_table(specs: Sequence[ScheduleInputs],
                          beta: float = POWER_BETA,
                          energy_cap: float = ENERGY_CAP_M,
                          mu_ratio: float = 1.0) -> Dict[PowerSchedule, List[float]]:
    """Per-seed energies for every schedule (rows = schedules)."""
    return {
        PowerSchedule(sched): EnergyComputer(
            sched, beta=beta, energy_cap=energy_cap, mu_ratio=mu_ratio
        ).compute_all(specs)
        for sched in SCHEDULE_ORDER
    }

"""AFLFast's Markov-chain bookkeeping and the AFLFast fuzzer itself.

This module supplies the *state* half of AFLFast: the counters that the
power schedules in :mod:`fuzzsim.aflfast_schedules` consume.

:class:`PathFrequencyTracker` implements the Markov chain of the paper.
A *state* is an execution path, identified -- exactly as AFL identifies a
"unique path" -- by the hash of the classified coverage trace.  For every
execution the tracker records

* ``f(i)``: how many generated inputs exercised state ``i``,
* ``s(i)``: how many times a seed exercising state ``i`` was selected,
* ``T(i, j)``: how many times mutating a seed of state ``i`` produced an
  input of state ``j``, from which the transition probabilities
  ``P(i, j) = T(i, j) / sum_k T(i, k)`` are estimated.

Rare paths (``f(i)`` far below the queue mean ``mu``) are flagged and given
an energy bonus, since they are the states from which undiscovered
neighbours are most likely reachable.

:class:`AFLFastFuzzer` subclasses :class:`fuzzsim.afl_fuzzer.AFLFuzzer` and
changes exactly the two things AFLFast changes:

1. ``power_schedule`` -- energy now comes from the selected
   :class:`~fuzzsim.aflfast_schedules.PowerSchedule` instead of being AFL's
   constant perf score;
2. seed selection order -- FAST/COE walk the queue in increasing ``s(i)``
   (:func:`prioritize_small_s`), the other schedules in increasing ``f(i)``
   (:func:`prioritize_small_f`).

Everything else (bitmap, calibration, trimming, culling, deterministic /
havoc / splice stages) is inherited untouched.

Determinism: all randomness still comes from the inherited
``numpy.random.RandomState`` seeded by the caller.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Any, Dict, List, Optional, Sequence, Set, Tuple

from fuzzsim.afl_fuzzer import (AFLFuzzer, ExecResult, MAP_SIZE, QueueEntry,
                                classify_counts, hash_trace)
from fuzzsim.aflfast_schedules import (ENERGY_CAP_M, EnergyComputer, POWER_BETA,
                                       PowerSchedule, RARE_PATH_BONUS,
                                       RARE_PATH_RATIO, S_PRIORITIZED_SCHEDULES,
                                       ScheduleInputs)

#: How many consecutive COE cut-offs we tolerate before forcing a seed to be
#: fuzzed anyway.  ``mu`` is a mean, so some seed always survives the
#: cut-off, but the favored-skip lottery in ``select_next`` may keep passing
#: it over; this guard keeps the main loop from spinning without progress.
MAX_CUTOFF_STREAK = 64


class PathFrequencyTracker:
    """Markov chain over execution paths: ``f(i)``, ``s(i)`` and ``T(i, j)``.

    States are identified by the hash of a classified coverage trace, so
    two inputs share a state exactly when AFL would call them the same
    path.  Frequencies are exposed both raw (``frequency``) and relative to
    the queue mean (``relative_frequency``); the schedules consume the
    relative form so that energies do not drift as the campaign runs.
    """

    def __init__(self,
                 rare_ratio: float = RARE_PATH_RATIO,
                 rare_bonus: float = RARE_PATH_BONUS):
        self.rare_ratio = float(rare_ratio)
        self.rare_bonus_factor = float(rare_bonus)

        self.freq: Dict[str, int] = {}          # f(i)
        self.selections: Dict[str, int] = {}    # s(i)
        self.transitions: Dict[Tuple[str, str], int] = {}   # T(i, j)
        self.out_degree: Dict[str, int] = {}    # sum_k T(i, k)
        self.first_seen: Dict[str, int] = {}    # execution index of discovery
        self.total_executions = 0
        self.discovered_states = 0

    # -- state identification --------------------------------------------
    @staticmethod
    def state_id(trace: Dict[int, int]) -> str:
        """Markov state id of a trace: the hash of its classified form."""
        return hash_trace(classify_counts(trace))

    # -- recording --------------------------------------------------------
    def record_execution(self, state: str,
                         src_state: Optional[str] = None) -> str:
        """Count one input exercising ``state``, optionally as a transition.

        ``src_state`` is the state of the seed the input was mutated from;
        passing it records the Markov transition ``src_state -> state``.
        """
        self.total_executions += 1
        if state not in self.freq:
            self.freq[state] = 0
            self.first_seen[state] = self.total_executions
            self.discovered_states += 1
        self.freq[state] += 1
        if src_state is not None:
            self.record_transition(src_state, state)
        return state

    def observe(self, trace: Dict[int, int],
                src_state: Optional[str] = None) -> str:
        """Convenience wrapper: derive the state of ``trace`` and record it."""
        return self.record_execution(self.state_id(trace), src_state)

    def record_transition(self, src: str, dst: str) -> None:
        """Count one Markov transition ``src -> dst``."""
        key = (src, dst)
        self.transitions[key] = self.transitions.get(key, 0) + 1
        self.out_degree[src] = self.out_degree.get(src, 0) + 1

    def record_selection(self, state: str) -> int:
        """Count one selection of a seed exercising ``state`` (``s(i) += 1``)."""
        self.selections[state] = self.selections.get(state, 0) + 1
        return self.selections[state]

    # -- queries ----------------------------------------------------------
    def frequency(self, state: str) -> int:
        """``f(i)``: number of generated inputs that exercised ``state``."""
        return self.freq.get(state, 0)

    def selection_count(self, state: str) -> int:
        """``s(i)``: number of times a seed of ``state`` has been selected."""
        return self.selections.get(state, 0)

    def mu(self, states: Optional[Sequence[str]] = None) -> float:
        """``mu``: mean path frequency, over ``states`` or the whole chain."""
        keys = list(states) if states is not None else list(self.freq)
        if not keys:
            return 0.0
        return sum(self.frequency(k) for k in keys) / len(keys)

    def relative_frequency(self, state: str,
                           states: Optional[Sequence[str]] = None) -> float:
        """``f(i) / mu`` -- the scale-free frequency the schedules consume."""
        mean = self.mu(states)
        if mean <= 0.0:
            return 0.0
        return self.frequency(state) / mean

    def transition_probability(self, src: str, dst: str) -> float:
        """Maximum-likelihood estimate of ``P(src -> dst)``."""
        total = self.out_degree.get(src, 0)
        if total <= 0:
            return 0.0
        return self.transitions.get((src, dst), 0) / total

    def transition_matrix(self) -> Dict[str, Dict[str, float]]:
        """Full estimated transition matrix ``P`` as nested dicts."""
        matrix: Dict[str, Dict[str, float]] = {}
        for (src, dst), count in self.transitions.items():
            total = self.out_degree.get(src, 0) or 1
            matrix.setdefault(src, {})[dst] = count / total
        return matrix

    def self_transition_probability(self, state: str) -> float:
        """``P(i, i)``: how sticky a state is (AFLFast's core inefficiency)."""
        return self.transition_probability(state, state)

    # -- rare paths -------------------------------------------------------
    def is_rare(self, state: str,
                states: Optional[Sequence[str]] = None) -> bool:
        """A path is rare when ``f(i) < rare_ratio * mu``."""
        return self.relative_frequency(state, states) < self.rare_ratio

    def rare_states(self, states: Optional[Sequence[str]] = None) -> List[str]:
        """Every known state that currently counts as rare, sorted."""
        keys = list(states) if states is not None else sorted(self.freq)
        return [k for k in keys if self.is_rare(k, states)]

    def rare_bonus(self, state: str,
                   states: Optional[Sequence[str]] = None) -> float:
        """Energy multiplier for ``state``: the bonus if rare, else 1."""
        return self.rare_bonus_factor if self.is_rare(state, states) else 1.0

    def stats(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Snapshot of the chain, for reports and tests."""
        return {
            "states": len(self.freq),
            "executions": self.total_executions,
            "transitions": len(self.transitions),
            "mu": self.mu(),
            "max_frequency": max(self.freq.values()) if self.freq else 0,
            "min_frequency": min(self.freq.values()) if self.freq else 0,
        }


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Seed prioritization strategies
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

def _entry_state(entry: QueueEntry) -> str:
    """Markov state of a queue entry (its calibration checksum)."""
    return entry.exec_cksum


def prioritize_small_s(entries: Sequence[QueueEntry],
                       tracker: PathFrequencyTracker) -> List[QueueEntry]:
    """Order the queue by increasing ``s(i)`` -- used by FAST and COE.

    Both schedules grow energy in ``s(i)``, so visiting the least-selected
    seeds first keeps the exponential from running away on one seed and
    gives every state at least one cheap visit before any state gets an
    expensive one.  Ties break on queue index, keeping the order stable.
    """
    return sorted(entries,
                  key=lambda e: (tracker.selection_count(_entry_state(e)),
                                 e.index))


def prioritize_small_f(entries: Sequence[QueueEntry],
                       tracker: PathFrequencyTracker) -> List[QueueEntry]:
    """Order the queue by increasing ``f(i)`` -- explore / linear / quad.

    Those schedules do not grow with ``s(i)`` fast enough to escape a
    high-density region on their own, so the *ordering* carries the
    exploration pressure: least-exercised path first.  Ties break on queue
    index.
    """
    return sorted(entries,
                  key=lambda e: (tracker.frequency(_entry_state(e)), e.index))


def prioritize_queue_order(entries: Sequence[QueueEntry],
                           tracker: PathFrequencyTracker) -> List[QueueEntry]:
    """AFL's own FIFO order -- used by EXPLOIT, which is plain AFL."""
    return list(entries)


#: Which prioritization strategy each schedule uses.
PRIORITIZERS = {
    PowerSchedule.EXPLOIT: prioritize_queue_order,
    PowerSchedule.EXPLORE: prioritize_small_f,
    PowerSchedule.COE: prioritize_small_s,
    PowerSchedule.FAST: prioritize_small_s,
    PowerSchedule.LINEAR: prioritize_small_f,
    PowerSchedule.QUAD: prioritize_small_f,
}


def prioritizer_for(schedule: PowerSchedule):
    """Return the prioritization function belonging to ``schedule``."""
    schedule = PowerSchedule(schedule)
    if schedule in S_PRIORITIZED_SCHEDULES:
        return prioritize_small_s
    return PRIORITIZERS[schedule]


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The fuzzer
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

class AFLFastFuzzer(AFLFuzzer):
    """AFL with an AFLFast power schedule and Markov-aware seed ordering."""

    def __init__(self,
                 target: Any,
                 seeds: Sequence[bytes],
                 seed: int = 42,
                 dictionary: Optional[Sequence[bytes]] = None,
                 skip_deterministic: bool = False,
                 max_execs: int = 20000,
                 map_size: int = MAP_SIZE,
                 use_splicing: bool = True,
                 total_edges: Optional[int] = None,
                 schedule: PowerSchedule = PowerSchedule.FAST,
                 beta: float = POWER_BETA,
                 energy_cap: float = ENERGY_CAP_M,
                 rare_ratio: float = RARE_PATH_RATIO,
                 rare_bonus: float = RARE_PATH_BONUS,
                 use_prioritization: bool = True):
        self.schedule = PowerSchedule(schedule)
        self.tracker = PathFrequencyTracker(rare_ratio=rare_ratio,
                                            rare_bonus=rare_bonus)
        self.energy_computer = EnergyComputer(self.schedule, beta=beta,
                                              energy_cap=energy_cap,
                                              rare_ratio=rare_ratio,
                                              rare_bonus=rare_bonus)
        self.prioritize = prioritizer_for(self.schedule)
        self.use_prioritization = use_prioritization

        # Bookkeeping for the experiment / reports.
        self.energy_log: List[float] = []
        self.energy_by_entry: Dict[int, List[float]] = {}
        self.cutoff_skips = 0
        self._cutoff_streak = 0
        self._current_state: Optional[str] = None

        super().__init__(target=target, seeds=seeds, seed=seed,
                         dictionary=dictionary,
                         skip_deterministic=skip_deterministic,
                         max_execs=max_execs, map_size=map_size,
                         use_splicing=use_splicing, total_edges=total_edges)

    # -- Markov bookkeeping ----------------------------------------------
    def run_target(self, data: bytes) -> ExecResult:
        """Run the target and fold the result into the Markov chain.

        Every execution -- calibration, deterministic stage, havoc, splice
        or trim -- contributes to ``f(i)``, and every execution performed
        while fuzzing a seed also contributes the transition
        ``state(seed) -> state(mutant)``.
        """
        res = super().run_target(data)
        self.tracker.observe(res.trace, src_state=self._current_state)
        return res

    def queue_states(self) -> List[str]:
        """Markov states currently represented in the queue."""
        return [_entry_state(e) for e in self.queue if e.exec_cksum]

    def entry_inputs(self, entry: QueueEntry) -> ScheduleInputs:
        """Bundle ``(alpha, f/mu, s)`` for ``entry`` for the schedule."""
        states = self.queue_states()
        state = _entry_state(entry)
        return ScheduleInputs(
            alpha=self.calculate_score(entry),
            freq=self.tracker.relative_frequency(state, states),
            sel=self.tracker.selection_count(state) or entry.n_fuzz,
        )

    # -- energy -----------------------------------------------------------
    def power_schedule(self, entry: QueueEntry) -> float:
        """AFLFast energy: the selected schedule applied to ``(alpha, f, s)``.

        ``alpha`` is AFL's own perf score, so AFLFast inherits AFL's speed /
        size / depth heuristics and only re-weights them by the Markov
        statistics.  The rare-path bonus is applied inside the
        :class:`~fuzzsim.aflfast_schedules.EnergyComputer`.
        """
        return self.energy_computer.energy_of(self.entry_inputs(entry))

    def schedule_energies(self) -> List[float]:
        """Energy the schedule would assign to each queue entry right now."""
        specs = [self.entry_inputs(e) for e in self.queue]
        return self.energy_computer.compute_all(specs)

    # -- seed selection ---------------------------------------------------
    def _skip_entry(self, entry: QueueEntry) -> bool:
        """AFL's favored-seed lottery, unchanged (see ``AFLFuzzer.select_next``)."""
        from fuzzsim.afl_fuzzer import (SKIP_NFAV_NEW_PROB, SKIP_NFAV_OLD_PROB,
                                        SKIP_TO_NEW_PROB)
        if self.pending_favored:
            return ((entry.was_fuzzed or not entry.favored)
                    and self._rand_below(100) < SKIP_TO_NEW_PROB)
        if not entry.favored and len(self.queue) > 10:
            if not entry.was_fuzzed:
                return self._rand_below(100) < SKIP_NFAV_NEW_PROB
            return self._rand_below(100) < SKIP_NFAV_OLD_PROB
        return False

    def select_next(self, cursor: int) -> Tuple[Optional[QueueEntry], int]:
        """Walk the *prioritized* queue, keeping AFL's favored-skip lottery."""
        if not self.use_prioritization:
            return super().select_next(cursor)
        order = self.prioritize(self.queue, self.tracker)
        n = len(order)
        if n == 0:
            return None, 0
        for step in range(n):
            idx = (cursor + step) % n
            entry = order[idx]
            if self._skip_entry(entry):
                continue
            return entry, (idx + 1) % n
        return order[cursor % n], (cursor + 1) % n

    # -- main loop --------------------------------------------------------
    def fuzz_one(self, entry: QueueEntry) -> int:
        """Fuzz one seed with the schedule's energy, honouring COE's cut-off."""
        entry.times_chosen += 1
        entry.n_fuzz += 1
        state = _entry_state(entry)
        self.tracker.record_selection(state)
        self._current_state = state
        try:
            energy = self.power_schedule(entry)
            entry.perf_score = energy
            self.energy_log.append(energy)
            self.energy_by_entry.setdefault(entry.index, []).append(energy)

            # COE cut-off: an above-average path gets nothing at all.  The
            # streak guard stops the main loop spinning if the favored
            # lottery keeps handing us cut-off seeds.
            if energy <= 0.0 and self._cutoff_streak < MAX_CUTOFF_STREAK:
                self._cutoff_streak += 1
                self.cutoff_skips += 1
                return 0
            self._cutoff_streak = 0

            if not entry.trim_done:
                self.trim_case(entry)

            found = 0
            doing_det = not self.skip_deterministic and not entry.passed_det
            if doing_det:
                found += self.deterministic_stages(entry)
            found += self.havoc_stage(entry, energy, doing_det)
            found += self.splice_stage(entry, energy)

            if not entry.was_fuzzed:
                entry.was_fuzzed = True
                self.pending_not_fuzzed = max(0, self.pending_not_fuzzed - 1)
                if entry.favored:
                    self.pending_favored = max(0, self.pending_favored - 1)
            entry.fuzz_count += 1
            return found
        finally:
            self._current_state = None

    # -- reporting --------------------------------------------------------
    def stats(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        stats = super().stats()
        energies = self.schedule_energies()
        stats.update({
            "schedule": self.schedule.value,
            "markov_states": len(self.tracker.freq),
            "markov_transitions": len(self.tracker.transitions),
            "mu": self.tracker.mu(self.queue_states()),
            "cutoff_skips": self.cutoff_skips,
            "energy_assignments": len(self.energy_log),
            "mean_assigned_energy": (sum(self.energy_log) / len(self.energy_log)
                                     if self.energy_log else 0.0),
            "queue_energies": energies,
            "energy_summary": self.energy_computer.summary(
                [self.entry_inputs(e) for e in self.queue]),
            "rare_states": len(self.tracker.rare_states(self.queue_states())),
        })
        return stats

    def path_frequencies(self) -> Dict[str, int]:
        """``f(i)`` for every queue state, keyed by state id."""
        return {s: self.tracker.frequency(s) for s in self.queue_states()}

    def selection_counts(self) -> Dict[str, int]:
        """``s(i)`` for every queue state, keyed by state id."""
        return {s: self.tracker.selection_count(s) for s in self.queue_states()}

    def covered_edge_set(self) -> Set[int]:
        return self.covered_edges()

"""AFLFast experiment: Markov-chain power schedules on the 'crashme' target.

Runs the same corpus / budget / dictionary as the AFL baseline experiment
through :class:`~fuzzsim.aflfast_search.AFLFastFuzzer` under two of the
paper's schedules and reports:

``AFLFAST_PATHS_FAST``
    Queue length after a FAST-schedule campaign.

``AFLFAST_PATHS_COE``
    Queue length after a COE-schedule campaign.

``AFLFAST_SPEEDUP``
    *Path-discovery throughput* of AFLFast (FAST) relative to AFL, i.e.

        ``(paths_aflfast / execs_aflfast) / (paths_afl / execs_afl)``

    Both fuzzers are given the identical execution budget, so this is the
    ratio of paths found per execution -- the "exponentially faster path
    discovery" quantity of the paper, measured at equal cost.  A value of
    1.00 means AFLFast bought the same number of paths for the same number
    of executions; the target saturates its reachable path set long before
    the budget runs out, so no schedule can buy more.  (The alternative
    "executions needed to reach N paths" definition is also computed and
    printed with ``--verbose``: FAST gets to the tenth path noticeably
    sooner, but once both have saturated, throughput at equal budget is the
    fair comparison.)

``AFLFAST_MEAN_ENERGY``
    Mean energy the FAST schedule assigns to the entries of its final
    corpus, i.e. ``mean_i p(i)`` over the whole queue, evaluated with the
    final ``f(i)`` / ``s(i)`` statistics.  This is the distribution whose
    Gini coefficient is reported by ``--verbose``.

Emits ``EXPERIMENT_NAME: VALUE`` lines consumed by run.sh.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Tuple

from fuzzsim.aflfast_schedules import (ENERGY_CAP_M, POWER_BETA, PowerSchedule,
                                       SCHEDULE_ORDER, compare_schedules,
                                       describe_schedule)
from fuzzsim.aflfast_search import AFLFastFuzzer
from fuzzsim.experiments.afl_experiment import DICTIONARY, INITIAL_SEEDS, run_afl
from fuzzsim.targets.crashme import CrashmeProgram

SEED = 42
MAX_EXECS = 30000


def run_aflfast(schedule: PowerSchedule = PowerSchedule.FAST,
                seed: int = SEED,
                max_execs: int = MAX_EXECS,
                beta: float = POWER_BETA,
                energy_cap: float = ENERGY_CAP_M) -> Dict[str, object]:
    """Run one AFLFast campaign under ``schedule`` on the crashme target."""
    target = CrashmeProgram()
    fuzzer = AFLFastFuzzer(
        target=target,
        seeds=INITIAL_SEEDS,
        seed=seed,
        dictionary=DICTIONARY,
        max_execs=max_execs,
        total_edges=target.get_total_edges(),
        schedule=schedule,
        beta=beta,
        energy_cap=energy_cap,
    )
    stats = fuzzer.run()
    stats["fuzzer"] = fuzzer
    return stats


def path_throughput(stats: Dict[str, object]) -> float:
    """Paths discovered per execution."""
    execs = int(stats["total_execs"])  # type: ignore[arg-type]
    if execs <= 0:
        return 0.0
    return int(stats["paths_total"]) / execs  # type: ignore[arg-type]


def throughput_speedup(fast_stats: Dict[str, object],
                       afl_stats: Dict[str, object]) -> float:
    """Ratio of AFLFast's path-discovery throughput to AFL's."""
    base = path_throughput(afl_stats)
    if base <= 0.0:
        return 0.0
    return path_throughput(fast_stats) / base


def execs_to_paths(path_history: List[Tuple[int, int]],
                   n_paths: int) -> Optional[int]:
    """Executions the campaign needed to reach ``n_paths`` queue entries."""
    for execs, paths in path_history:
        if paths >= n_paths:
            return execs
    return None


def execs_to_paths_speedup(fast_stats: Dict[str, object],
                           afl_stats: Dict[str, object]) -> Optional[float]:
    """Alternative speedup: execs AFL needed / execs AFLFast needed.

    Measured at the common path count both fuzzers reached.
    """
    fast_fuzzer = fast_stats["fuzzer"]
    afl_fuzzer = afl_stats["fuzzer"]
    common = min(int(fast_stats["paths_total"]),  # type: ignore[arg-type]
                 int(afl_stats["paths_total"]))  # type: ignore[arg-type]
    a = execs_to_paths(afl_fuzzer.path_history, common)  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
    b = execs_to_paths(fast_fuzzer.path_history, common)  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
    if not a or not b:
        return None
    return a / b


def mean_queue_energy(stats: Dict[str, object]) -> float:
    """Mean energy assigned to the final corpus by the run's schedule."""
    energies = stats["queue_energies"]  # type: ignore[index]
    if not energies:
        return 0.0
    return sum(energies) / len(energies)  # type: ignore[arg-type]


def main() -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="AFLFast power schedules")
    parser.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=SEED)
    parser.add_argument("--max-execs", type=int, default=MAX_EXECS)
    parser.add_argument("--beta", type=float, default=POWER_BETA)
    parser.add_argument("--energy-cap", type=float, default=ENERGY_CAP_M)
    parser.add_argument("--verbose", action="store_true")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    fast = run_aflfast(PowerSchedule.FAST, seed=args.seed,
                       max_execs=args.max_execs, beta=args.beta,
                       energy_cap=args.energy_cap)
    coe = run_aflfast(PowerSchedule.COE, seed=args.seed,
                      max_execs=args.max_execs, beta=args.beta,
                      energy_cap=args.energy_cap)
    baseline = run_afl(seed=args.seed, max_execs=args.max_execs)

    speedup = throughput_speedup(fast, baseline)
    mean_energy = mean_queue_energy(fast)

    print(f"AFLFAST_PATHS_FAST: {fast['paths_total']}")
    print(f"AFLFAST_PATHS_COE: {coe['paths_total']}")
    print(f"AFLFAST_SPEEDUP: {speedup:.2f}")
    print(f"AFLFAST_MEAN_ENERGY: {mean_energy:.1f}")

    if args.verbose:
        alt = execs_to_paths_speedup(fast, baseline)
        fast_fuzzer: AFLFastFuzzer = fast["fuzzer"]  # type: ignore[assignment]
        coe_fuzzer: AFLFastFuzzer = coe["fuzzer"]  # type: ignore[assignment]
        summary = fast["energy_summary"]  # type: ignore[index]
        print(f"  beta / M            : {args.beta} / {args.energy_cap}")
        print(f"  fast coverage       : {fast['coverage_pct']:.1f}%")
        print(f"  coe coverage        : {coe['coverage_pct']:.1f}%")
        print(f"  fast crashes        : {fast['unique_crashes']}")
        print(f"  coe crashes         : {coe['unique_crashes']}")
        print(f"  execs (fast/coe/afl): {fast['total_execs']} / "
              f"{coe['total_execs']} / {baseline['total_execs']}")
        print(f"  execs-to-10-paths   : fast="
              f"{execs_to_paths(fast_fuzzer.path_history, 10)} afl="
              f"{execs_to_paths(baseline['fuzzer'].path_history, 10)}"  # type: ignore[index]
              f" (ratio {alt:.2f})" if alt else "")
        print(f"  markov states       : {fast['markov_states']}")
        print(f"  markov transitions  : {fast['markov_transitions']}")
        print(f"  mu (queue mean f)   : {fast['mu']:.1f}")
        print(f"  rare queue states   : {fast['rare_states']}")
        print(f"  energy gini (fast)  : {summary['gini']:.3f}")
        print(f"  energy gini (coe)   : "
              f"{coe['energy_summary']['gini']:.3f}")  # type: ignore[index]
        print(f"  coe cut-off skips   : {coe['cutoff_skips']}")
        print(f"  fast queue energies : "
              f"{[round(e, 2) for e in fast['queue_energies']]}")  # type: ignore[index]
        print(f"  coe queue energies  : "
              f"{[round(e, 2) for e in coe['queue_energies']]}")  # type: ignore[index]
        print(f"  fast selections s(i): {sorted(fast_fuzzer.selection_counts().values())}")
        print(f"  coe selections s(i) : {sorted(coe_fuzzer.selection_counts().values())}")
        print("  schedule formulas:")
        for sched in SCHEDULE_ORDER:
            print(f"    {sched.value:<8}: {describe_schedule(sched)}")
        specs = fast_fuzzer.queue_inputs()
        print("  same queue, every schedule (mean / gini):")
        for sched, stats in compare_schedules(specs, beta=args.beta,
                                              energy_cap=args.energy_cap).items():
            print(f"    {sched.value:<8}: mean={stats['mean']:8.2f} "
                  f"gini={stats['gini']:.3f} zero={stats['zero_fraction']:.2f}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
